source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Locally blocking neuromuscular transmission at the injection site, reducing spasticity in that specific targeted muscle","B":"Carrying fairly little established role in managing focal spasticity despite being commonly used for this exact purpose","C":"Curing the client's underlying neurological condition itself, rather than managing one of its associated symptoms","D":"Producing a systemic relaxation of essentially every muscle throughout the client's entire body"}}
source_row.rationale: Botulinum toxin injections work by locally blocking neuromuscular transmission at the specific injection site, reducing spasticity in that targeted muscle group, offering a more focal treatment approach compared to systemic oral antispasmodic medications, though effects are temporary and require repeat injections.
source_row.source_detail: Local Mechanism of Botulinum Toxin for Spasticity
